source_text: Nihil ergo per Legem Dei agi potest contra Deum Legis auctorem. Quo uno compendio excluditur quidem quidquid ab errantibus consuevit obici; sed nos ad docendum quam sit veritas locuples cui credimus, illis quoque Scripturarum locis, quae intellectum sententiae elocutionum perplexitate velarunt, expositionis lucem solemus afferre; ut originis suae dignitatem reserata possideant, nec ab stemmate sacro velut notha aut degenerantia separentur.
pass_a_gloss: Nothing therefore can be done through the Law of God against God the author of the Law. By which one shortcut whatever those in error have been accustomed to object is indeed shut out; but we, to teach how rich is the truth to which we believe, are accustomed to bring the light of exposition also to those places of the Scriptures which have veiled the understanding of the sentence by the entanglement of expressions; so that, unbarred, they may possess the dignity of their origin, and not be separated from the sacred stem as if spurious or degenerating.

lemmas.lexica: LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Nothing, then, can be done through God's Law against God, the author of the Law. This single brief argument rules out whatever those in error usually object. Nevertheless, to show how rich is the truth we believe, we also bring the light of explanation to passages of Scripture whose tangled wording has veiled their meaning. Once opened up, they may retain the dignity of their origin, rather than being cut off from their sacred ancestry as though they were illegitimate or degenerate offspring.

choices.why: Julian's sacred writings; keep Scripture, not 'Bible' as a later book-name.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
